ai.title: Keep Freebuff session slot during npm launcher update restart
ai.summary: The CLI now recognizes when a SIGTERM is issued by the npm launcher during an in-place binary update instead of a manual user kill. In Freebuff mode, the process calls `isLauncherUpdateTermination` to verify the parent process is a live launcher, then sets `keepSlotForRelaunch` in the session store so subsequent `releaseSlot` calls become no-ops. This mechanism allows the relaunched binary to take over the existing paid session state on startup rather than treating the interruption as a crash or normal exit, preventing users from losing their active model hour mid-update.

ai.title: Add ripgrep extraction with cache fallback for read-only installs
ai.summary: The CLI now extracts the ripgrep binary using a new `extractRipgrep` function that atomically publishes complete, executable binaries. When the installation directory is not writable due to `EACCES`, `EPERM`, or `EROFS` errors, the function falls back to a cache directory. This cache is keyed by the `sha256` digest of the binary to ensure upgrades do not reuse stale bytes.

ai.title: CLI adds multi-session identity, relaunch handoff, and capacity
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI now uses private multi-session claims with a `cli:` prefixed instance ID for non-limited-offer models, allowing concurrent CLI and Desktop sessions to share account capacity instead of superseding each other. New modules `freebuff-session-identity.ts` and `freebuff-session-relaunch.ts` handle per-purchase identity generation and launcher-scoped session handoff for deferred updates. The takeover prompt in the landing screen now supports capacity-based takeovers with a "Choose model" back option, and the session store tracks pending admissions to cancel unacknowledged POSTs on exit. This changes the session lifecycle from single-instance per account to multi-instance with explicit user confirmation when capacity limits are reached.

eli5.text: The Freebuff assistant now shows your past conversations in a read-only view when you press a shortcut, letting you scroll through saved history without needing an active session or the ability to send new messages. In addition, every ad now carries only two anonymous identifiers pointing to the conversation it appears in; no message text or code is sent along, and the system keeps track of interrupted runs so the next ad does not accidentally reference a task that never finished.

entries.title: CLI update: sponsored-run
entries.summary: CLI, Shared/Core changes across 2 file(s) (+143/−3).

ai.title: Sponsored compute grant expiry anchored to run start
ai.summary: The sponsored compute grant lifecycle in `common/src/ads/sponsored-compute-contract.ts` now anchors the active spending window to when the run starts rather than when it is accepted. Two new constants, `SPONSORED_COMPUTE_RUN_WINDOW_MS` (one hour) and `SPONSORED_COMPUTE_START_DEADLINE_MS` (matching the run token TTL), define these bounds, and a new `sponsoredComputeRunDeadlineMs` helper calculates the effective deadline as the minimum of the grant expiry and the start time plus the run window. In `cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts`, the `SponsoredRun` class now uses this helper to set its local abort timer, preventing the grant from expiring during the wait for the conversation to be free. This change ensures that queued runs retain their full hour of compute time once they actually begin.
ai.evidence: The diff adds `SPONSORED_COMPUTE_RUN_WINDOW_MS` and `SPONSORED_COMPUTE_START_DEADLINE_MS` to `common/src/ads/sponsored-compute-contract.ts`, and updates `startTurn` in `cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts` to use the new `sponsoredComputeRunDeadlineMs` helper for the grant expiry timer.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side implementation of the brought-in deadline logic, only the client-side constants and helper.

changes.what: Introduced `SPONSORED_COMPUTE_RUN_WINDOW_MS` and `SPONSORED_COMPUTE_START_DEADLINE_MS` constants and the `sponsoredComputeRunDeadlineMs` function to anchor grant expiry to run start.
Updated `SponsoredRun.startTurn` to use `sponsoredComputeRunDeadlineMs` for the grant expiry timer instead of the raw `expiresAtMs`.

eli5.text: Sponsored tasks now get their full one-hour run window starting from when the task actually begins, not from when you accepted it. This prevents the time limit from expiring while the task waits in the queue for your other work to finish, which previously caused some sponsored tasks to fail before they could start or get cut off mid-run. The change affects the internal behavior of advertiser-funded tasks in the terminal assistant; you will not notice any new features or settings, but sponsored tasks are less likely to fail due to waiting.

entries.title: CLI update: sponsored-agent
entries.summary: CLI changes across 1 file(s) (+64/−53).

ai.title: Sponsored in-place run prompts harden against task hijacking
ai.summary: The system prompt sections for in-place sponsored runs in `cli/src/utils/sponsored-agent.ts` now explicitly mark conversation context as read-only and forbid resuming, retrying, or completing any user requests mentioned in that context. This change follows `COD-665` trace reviews that showed models interpreting sponsored procedures as untrusted distractors or prompt injections, leading to inconsistent execution. The updated `SPONSORED_TASK_FRAMING` names the procedure as the turn's sole goal to prevent the model from weighing it as secondary to the conversation.
ai.evidence: The diff in `cli/src/utils/sponsored-agent.ts` modifies `SPONSORED_TASK_FRAMING` and `SPONSORED_CONTEXT_HEADING` constants, adding read-only restrictions and prohibiting the resumption of pending user requests, while citing `COD-665` trace review findings where models treated procedures as 'prompt injection' or 'distractor'.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the Desktop-side changes in `freebuff-desktop` that are mirrored in these constants, nor the specific test file assertions that pin the shared bytes.

eli5.text: The instructions given to the AI assistant during a sponsored run in the terminal are now stricter, explicitly marking your recent chat history as read-only background and forbidding the assistant from resuming or completing any tasks you mentioned in those messages. This change ensures the AI focuses solely on the advertised procedure and does not get distracted by trying to finish other work, making the execution of sponsored runs more consistent and predictable. The effect is that the assistant will not attempt to pick up unfinished tasks from your chat while performing a paid advertisement task.
